description: Electronic narrative operator log, shift turnover, operator rounds data on rugged tablets, and access to plant data displays on the business network
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Logs and rounds data are required records; paper fallback is workable for one day before data quality and turnover suffer. The unit itself keeps operating because Level 3 and Level 4 do not depend on the business network
manual_workaround: Paper narrative log and paper rounds sheets kept in the control room; controlled hard-copy procedures; plant data from Level 3 control room displays only
dependent_people_or_facilities: Licensed operators; control room; work control center
quantified_operational_impact: About 400 rounds readings per shift move to paper and are back-entered later (about 30 staff-hours per day)
quantified_regulatory_impact: Operator log and rounds records must be complete; late entries flagged for review under the operations administrative procedure
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: trending of equipment readings is delayed; no nuclear safety function depends on the business network
regulatory_linkage: 73.54 defensive architecture keeps Level 3 and 4 independent of this process (CSP)

description: Prepare, approve, hang, and release equipment clearances that protect workers; the WMS clearance and tagging module prints tags and tracks clearance status
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Worker protection depends on accurate clearance status. During a refueling outage about 140 clearances a day are active and most critical-path work needs a new or changed clearance; 8 hours is one work shift. RPO 15 minutes because a lost clearance status change is a safety hazard
manual_workaround: Paper clearance process with pre-printed blank tags, a manual clearance log in the work control center, and independent verification of each tag in the field
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (clearance and tagging module on 2 legacy servers); SYS-03; SYS-06
dependent_people_or_facilities: Work control center; operations clearance coordinators; maintenance crews
quantified_operational_impact: Outage: about half of critical-path work stops for one shift (about $2.03 million per outage day); online: about 25 clearances a day handled on paper
quantified_regulatory_impact: Clearance errors are entered in the CAP; an event with worker injury may be reportable under OSHA rules
safety_impact_detail: Severe: an incorrect or lost clearance can expose a worker to energized or pressurized equipment
regulatory_linkage: Not a CDA under the CSP analysis (clearances are verified in the field), but its integrity is a personnel safety control

business_process: Work order planning, scheduling, and refueling outage control
description: Work packages, the integrated outage schedule, and critical path tracking in the WMS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Outage extension costs about $2.03 million per day (lost generation plus contractor standby). Online, work can wait a day
manual_workaround: Printed 3-day look-ahead schedule and work packages staged the night before; outage control center whiteboards
dependent_people_or_facilities: Outage control center; planners; about 1,000 outage contractors
quantified_operational_impact: Outage productivity drops about 50% without the WMS; 24 hours equals about half a day of outage extension
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: work package errors increase when packages are assembled by hand
regulatory_linkage: Outage schedule protects refueling commitments; no direct regulatory clock

business_process: Corrective action program (CAP) entry, screening, and 73.77(b) recording
description: Record conditions adverse to quality and cyber security program deficiencies, screen them daily, and record 73.77 events within 24 hours
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: 10 CFR 73.77(b) requires vulnerabilities, weaknesses, failures, and deficiencies in the cyber security program, and 73.77(a) notifications, to be recorded in the site corrective action program within 24 hours of discovery
manual_workaround: None written today (gap 5). Proposed: paper CAP intake form with sequential numbers held by the CAP coordinator, entered when CAP is restored
quantified_operational_impact: About 35 condition reports a day (about 90 during an outage) need manual intake
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missing the 24-hour recording is a 73.77(b) noncompliance; a cyber attack on the business network makes this more likely exactly when it matters
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: delayed screening of conditions adverse to quality

description: Issue and retrieve current procedures, drawings, and licensing basis documents from the EDMS; verify revision before use
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Work cannot start without a current procedure; controlled hard copies cover the control room and emergency procedures but not most maintenance procedures
manual_workaround: Controlled hard copies in the control room, the TSC, and the EOF; document control desk issues printed copies verified against the last daily revision list
dependent_people_or_facilities: Document control desk; all work groups
quantified_operational_impact: About 600 procedure retrievals a day online and about 2,000 during an outage
quantified_regulatory_impact: Use of a superseded procedure is a condition adverse to quality entered in the CAP
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: risk of using a superseded procedure
regulatory_linkage: Document control under the quality assurance program; CSP records retention (73.54(h)) also depends on EDMS

business_process: Radiation work permits and dose tracking
description: Issue radiation work permits (RWPs), log entries to radiologically controlled areas, and track worker dose against limits and alarms
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Workers cannot enter radiologically controlled areas without an RWP and dose tracking; outage radiological work is heavy
manual_workaround: Paper RWPs and sign-in sheets; electronic dosimeters read at the access point and logged by hand; dose margins checked by RP technicians
dependent_people_or_facilities: RP technicians; radiologically controlled area access point
quantified_operational_impact: Outage: about 600 RCA entries a day; manual processing halves throughput at the access point
quantified_regulatory_impact: Occupational dose records must be accurate and complete; a dose tracking error can lead to an NRC violation
safety_impact_detail: Severe: undetected dose approaching an administrative or regulatory limit
regulatory_linkage: Radiation protection program; the system is classified as not a CDA in the CSP analysis

description: Background checks, fitness-for-duty results, and unescorted access decisions under the 73.56 program, including the industry shared access data system
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No one may be granted unescorted access until the access authorization process is complete; before an outage about 150 contractors a day are in-processed
manual_workaround: Escorted access only for workers not yet authorized; no paper path for granting unescorted access
dependent_third_parties: Industry shared access data system; background screening vendor; fitness-for-duty laboratory
quantified_operational_impact: About 150 contractors a day idle or under escort before and during the first week of an outage
quantified_regulatory_impact: Granting access without a complete process would violate 73.56
regulatory_linkage: C-NUCLEAR-S02 (73.56); personal information under Fla. Stat. 501.171 (C-NUCLEAR-S04)

business_process: Emergency response organization (ERO) callout and EOF readiness
description: Call out the ERO to staff the TSC, OSC, and EOF; EOF business LAN, phones, and email for offsite coordination
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Emergency plan staffing commitments start at the emergency declaration; the callout must work at any hour. RPO 24 hours for the roster (updated daily)
manual_workaround: Printed ERO call tree with personal phone numbers at the control room and security; EOF dedicated EP phones (not on the business network)
dependent_systems: SYS-14 (ERO callout service); SYS-04; SYS-06 (EOF business LAN)
dependent_third_parties: ERO callout service vendor; telecom carriers
quantified_operational_impact: About 120 ERO members on the roster; the manual call tree takes about 45 minutes versus 5 minutes
quantified_regulatory_impact: Failure to staff emergency facilities in the committed time is an emergency plan performance issue reviewed by the NRC
safety_impact_detail: Severe: delayed emergency staffing during an actual event
regulatory_linkage: 73.54(a)(1)(iii) emergency preparedness functions; the callout service was never evaluated by the CST (gap 3)

description: Engineering changes, including the 73.54(d)(3) cyber evaluation of modifications to CDAs, and design basis document updates
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Changes can wait days unless an emergent outage modification is on the critical path
manual_workaround: Defer non-emergent changes; emergent changes on paper with the CST signing the cyber evaluation
quantified_operational_impact: About 12 active design changes at a time; 3 days of engineering labor slowed
quantified_regulatory_impact: Modifications must be evaluated before implementation (73.54(d)(3))

business_process: Generation dispatch, telemetry, and scheduling with the Balancing Authority
description: Real-time MW and MVAR telemetry to the Balancing Authority through the dispatch RTU, dispatch instructions, and day-ahead schedules
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The Balancing Authority needs real-time telemetry; a manual phone process is acceptable to it for a few hours
manual_workaround: Recorded phone line between the control room and the Balancing Authority; hourly readings by phone
dependent_third_parties: Balancing Authority; telecom carrier; RTU vendor
quantified_operational_impact: Telemetry every few seconds replaced by hourly phone readings
quantified_regulatory_impact: Telemetry loss is coordinated with the Balancing Authority; CIP-003-9 incident response applies if a cyber cause is suspected

business_process: Generation data and settlement reporting (GDSR) for PPA-2
description: Daily hourly net generation and clean energy attribute data to the PPA-2 buyer; monthly settlement statements to both buyers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: PPA-2 allows late data with a service credit of $10,000 per late day; repeated failures threaten the buyer relationship
manual_workaround: Revenue meter readings by phone from the dispatch desk; spreadsheet calculation with a second reviewer
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; PPA-2 buyer data portal
quantified_operational_impact: One daily file and one monthly statement per buyer

business_process: PPA invoicing, payables, and cash management
description: Monthly invoices to both buyers, vendor payments, treasury
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Monthly cycle; about $37 million is invoiced each month, so a week of delay is a cash timing issue, not a loss
manual_workaround: Bank portal payments; invoices from the settlement spreadsheet

business_process: Parts issue, procurement, and quality records for safety-related items
description: Warehouse issues against work orders, purchase orders, receipt inspection records, and supplier qualification records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Outage parts issues on the critical path; online the warehouse can run on paper for days
manual_workaround: Paper issue tickets against printed work orders; receipt inspection on paper forms
quantified_operational_impact: Outage: about 1,500 parts issues a day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Quality records for safety-related items must be complete and retrievable
regulatory_linkage: CDA supply chain controls under the CSP (RG 5.71 C.12) depend on these records

description: Qualification records for operators, technicians, and security officers; licensed operator requalification tracking
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Qualification checks before task assignment can use the last printed qualification matrix for a week
manual_workaround: Weekly printed qualification matrix in each work group
quantified_regulatory_impact: Assigning an unqualified worker is a CAP condition and can be an NRC violation
regulatory_linkage: Cyber security training records (73.54(d)(1)) are kept here

description: Payroll, benefits, time and attendance, terminations feed to identity
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Biweekly payroll; the prior payroll can be repeated once
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll; paper time sheets

description: Email, chat, and file sharing for all staff; the main channel for outage coordination with contractors
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Work coordination slows sharply after one day, especially during an outage
manual_workaround: Phones and radios; outage control center briefings; printed contact lists

description: Licensee event reports, license amendment requests, responses to NRC inspections, and the CSP change process
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Written reports have deadlines measured in days (for example, the 60-day written follow-up under 73.77(d)); emergency notifications use the ENS telephone, which does not depend on the business network
manual_workaround: Prepare submittals on a standalone laptop; NRC electronic submission from a clean device
quantified_regulatory_impact: A missed written report deadline is a violation

business_process: Security force scheduling and program administration
description: Officer post scheduling, training and weapons qualification tracking, and non-SGI security program records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Post coverage must be maintained; schedules are printed a week ahead
manual_workaround: Printed weekly post schedule; supervisor call lists
quantified_regulatory_impact: Security plan staffing commitments; SGI is not processed on these systems (SYS-16 is standalone)
regulatory_linkage: C-NUCLEAR-S01 (SGI kept off the business network)
